## 🖇️  Connect your Claude Pro or Max subscription

If you have a Claude Pro or Max subscription, Plandex can use it when calling Anthropic models. You can use it in either Integrated Models Mode on Plandex Cloud, or in BYO Key Mode (whether on Cloud or self-hosting).

Assuming you're using Anthropic models (which the default model pack does), you'll be asked if you want to connect your Claude subscription the first time you run Plandex. Follow the instructions to connect.

[Learn more in the docs.](https://docs.plandex.ai/models/claude-subscription)

## −136,866 lines. 80% of the library deleted. We started over. The agent now writes Python in one persistent REPL, straight on Chrome DevTools Protocol. No DOM serializer, no action schema, nothing in between. Simplicity wins: it is now the [state-of-the-art web agent](https://browser-use.com/benchmarks). ``` ● task │ ● model writes a cell new_tab(url); bu.click(41); js(...) │ ● REPL runs it on Chrome (CDP) → output back to the model │ ✓ finish(result) ``` **Same models: up to 33 points higher, 2.7–5.2x cheaper, 2–3x faster.** ```bash uv add 'browser-use==1.0.0' export BROWSER_USE_API_KEY=bu_... # cloud.browser-use.com/new-api-key ``` ```python from browser_use import Agent print(Agent('Find the number of stars of the browser-use repo').run_sync().final_result()) ``` Pin with `==`. # Nanobrowser v0.3.0

Nanobrowser 0.3 is rebuilt from the ground up: one agent in the side panel, on top of a new browser control layer that clicks the right element, acts like a real user and reports what really happened.

## What's new

- **CDP.** The new browser control is rebuilt with chrome.debugger API, it uses CDP to interact with elements in web pages. It's more stable than the previous injected scripts solution.
- **One agent, one chat per tab.** The old planner and navigator are replaced by a single agent. Several tasks can run side by side, each in its own tab group.
- **You decide what it may do.** Ask mode (default) asks before the agent submits, sends, deletes or uploads; Auto mode goes ahead. Payments, passwords, codes and access grants are always handed to you. Set any site to Allow, Ask or Block.
- **More reliable actions.** Each element has an ID tied to that exact element, clicks and typing are real browser input, and every action is sent once and reports whether the page responded.
- **Any model with tool calling.** Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, OpenRouter, Grok, DeepSeek, Mistral, any OpenAI-compatible endpoint, Ollama and LM Studio. Pick the model and reasoning effort per chat; Test models in Settings checks which ones work.
- **Attachments and uploads.** Attach images, text files or a screenshot of the tab; the agent can upload your files to a page and save results (CSV, Markdown) to Downloads.
- **Shortcuts, voice and custom instructions.** Start saved prompts with `/`, speak with OpenAI's or Gemini's voice model, and tell the agent what to

Knowledge is now a first-class page tree (pages/notes/pins) with major tool upgrades: `knowledge_list`, line/section/grep-style reads in `knowledge_read`, list pinning (`kind: 'list'`), and a link index for counting/listing `[[links]]`. Apps can also sync external content via server APIs like `knowledge.upsertPage()`/`removePage()` and note upserts, with optional vector/hybrid search and chunked embeddings for very long pages.

### Knowledge Explorer + read-only Knowledge HTTP/JS client APIs (and SSE change stream)
Mastra Server now offers opt-in read-only Knowledge routes (tree/page/graph/search/activity) plus an SSE events stream, with matching `listKnowledge()` / `getKnowledge()` APIs in `@mastra/client-js`. These routes are scope-gated (and FGA-aware) and enable building Knowledge browsing UIs outside Studio, including link-count/link-edge endpoints when the store supports the link index.

### Durable agent continuity across API restarts (fencing + shared storage requirement)
Evented durable agents no longer stop when the API process shuts down: workers continue running, clean up, and free threads correctly, with improved run ownership isolation and safer cancellation semantics. To get true cross-process continuity you now need fencing-capable shared storage (e.g. `PostgresStore` from `@mastra/pg`) plus shared pubsub/lease infrastructure.

### Background tasks + MCP: resumable “input required” flows that survive reloads
Suspended background tool calls can now be resumed

When the agent has a database, including one AgentOS supplies, a native request persists a PAUSED run that shows up in the existing chat and Approvals views, and Resolve plus Continue Run delivers the decision back to the same native execution without replaying the prompt. ## Features

- Tracing now runs on `opentelemetry-api` alone and emits OpenTelemetry GenAI semantic-convention spans, so any OTLP backend reads them: a plain collector, Grafana Tempo, Sentry, Datadog, Honeycomb, PostHog, Jaeger, Arize Phoenix, Langfuse. Phoenix and the OpenInference packages are no longer required.
- One `chat {model}` CLIENT span per Instructor attempt, driven by Instructor hooks: per-attempt and total usage (input, output, cached and reasoning tokens) for both chat-completion and Responses shapes, `gen_ai.response.model`, attempt count, validation errors as events, `error.type` on failures. Totals also land on the agent span.
- `AgentConfig(name=...)` gives agents a stable span name (`invoke_agent {name}`); `using_conversation(conversation_id)` sets `gen_ai.conversation.id` on everything inside the block.
- `TracingConfig(hide_inputs, hide_outputs, max_attribute_length, openinference_attributes, llm_spans)` replaces ad-hoc keyword options, with environment equivalents `ATOMIC_AGENTS_TRACE_HIDE_INPUTS`, `ATOMIC_AGENTS_TRACE_HIDE_OUTPUTS`, `ATOMIC_AGENTS_TRACE_MAX_ATTRIBUTE_LENGTH` and `ATOMIC_AGENTS_TRACE_LLM_SPANS`. The `OPENINFERENCE_HIDE_*` variables still work as a fallback.
- Hiding is applied before serialization and wins over truncation. Under `hide_outputs` every exception is reduced to `<Type>: <N> attempts (__REDACTED__)` and traceback frames carry no source lines, so retry exhaustion cannot leak model output.
- Cancellation (`CancelledError`, `GeneratorExit`) is recorded as `atomic_agents.cancelled=true` with status UNSET on agent and tool spans

# Agent Zero — Release Notes

## Highlights

This is a large release that promotes core tools into standalone plugins, overhauls the welcome screen, hardens channel security, improves streaming and UI responsiveness, and adds new search, migration, and documentation capabilities.

---

## Tool Plugin Architecture

- **Extracted bundled tools into standalone plugins:** `wait`, `notify_user`, `search_engine`, `a2a_chat`, `scheduler`, `behavior_adjustment`, and the scheduler Tasks UI are now standard plugins, each with dedicated badge styling, log types, and prompt files.
- **Unified memory tools:** The four separate `memory_load`, `memory_save`, `memory_delete`, and `memory_forget` tools are consolidated into a single `memory` tool with an `action` argument, matching the action-dispatch pattern used by other tools.
- **Per-action tool permissions:** Profiles can now allow or deny individual operations across all 12 bundled multi-action tools (e.g., allow file reads but block writes, or allow listing scheduled tasks but block deletion). The Agent Editor shows grouped action controls with expandable entries.
- **Centralized boolean argument coercion** across all promoted and core tools, removing duplicated helpers and strict-validation error paths.
- **Dedicated badge rendering** for goal, document_query, skills, vision, browser, office, and computer_use_remote tool calls, each with distinct accent colors and descriptive headlines.
- **Dropped agent-name prefix** from all tool log headlines, warning rows, and fallback entries for cleaner chat output.
- **Added catalog thumbnail
